label: Postinfectious Syndromes and Long-Term Sequelae after Giardia Infections.
summary: Giardiasis, caused by the parasite Giardia duodenalis, is a common infection throughout the world. Acute infections can be asymptomatic, cause mild gastrointestinal symptoms, or be associated with severe, prolonged diarrhea. Most Giardia infections are self-limiting; however, a subset of symptomatic and asymptomatic persons experience infection-associated chronic conditions that can affect multiple body systems.
